title: Goodwin's lost banjo and meeting Smith at a Pearson Hall rehearsal
summary: Goodwin played banjo in Lovett's Dixieland band and met Smith at a rehearsal for a Pearson Hall job; Smith thanks Lovett.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Do you remember a few years ago we were looking for a banjo for you to play, we had to play one of these Roaring 20s scenes? We couldn't find one anywhere, could we or did we find one for you?
Yes.
Oh we did find one. Weren't you and I looking for one?
(Inaudible).
I played banjo with Baby Lovett's Dixieland band several times.
Yeah but you sold your banjo.
That's where I first met you at the --
88 Keys
At the (unintelligible).
No. Lovett did a thing out at Pearson Hall, and I met you at a rehearsal where we were rehearsing for Baby's --
Thats right.
-- band to go out to Pearson Hall.
Right, but why did you sell your banjo?
I didn't sell it, it just got lost somewhere on the road.
Oh it got lost.
I don't remember (unintelligible) -- it's been so long.
Well that's great. Of course Baby's responsible for my whole band because he introduced me to everybody on my band. God bless you for that.
Thank you.
You know I've never forgotten it.
Thank you very much, Art.
